description.narrative: Programmet är ett samarbete mellan polismyndigheter och syftar till att stärka den makedonska polisens kapacitet att uppfylla internationell praxis och normer för mänskliga rättigheter inom närpolisarbete och ungdomsrätt,

The overall objective is to contribute to the capacity-building of a democratic police service in North Macedonia, which protects human rights, is accountable to the law, ensures a high level of integrity of its police officers and can respond judiciously, proactively, and equally to the needs of all groups in society.

The project will focus on enhancing the capacity of North Macedonian Police to meet international best practices and human rights standards in juvenile justice and community policing practices. The theory of change is based on the presumption that the development of a democratic police service in the long term will contribute to enhanced public trust in the police, improved safety and security in communities and lower levels of corruption in the police service, as well as contribute to a lower number of committed crimes and assist in the fight against organised and trans-border crime.
Within the component of Community policing the objective is to improve crime prevention and the response to community safety needs. Within the component of Juvenile Justice, the objective is to improve investigations of juvenile cases, with a particular focus on interviews of children in contact with the law, ensuring they are carried out in accordance with international professional and human rights standards.
Expected results within Juvenile Justice are 1) Legislation and regulatory framework aligned with international standards, 2) System for specialised training on Juvenile Justice established, 3) Improved organisation, structure and facilities for juvenile justice cases and 4) Improved stakeholder coordination.
Expected results within Community policing are 1) Enabling legal and regulatory framework for community policing, 2) Strengthened MoI training system for community policing training, 3) Enhanced information security and protection of staff working with sensitive information and 4) Improved systems and tools for community policing.

In both Community Policing and Juvenile Justice, the project supported a transition from fragmented and preparatory approaches to structured, nationally owned reform processes.
During 2025- 2026, the project continued to strengthen the Ministry of Interiors (MoI) capacity and advance police reform.
Key achievements during the reported period under Juvenile justice objective included :
- development of a forensic interview curriculum based on the NICHD Protocol (an internationally recognized Protocol , which is evidence-based guide for conducting forensic interviews with children and vulnerable witnesses),
- certification of 16 trainers in forensic interview techniques (FIT)
- 60 investigators trained by the above trainers in FIT
- establishment of a child-friendly interview rooms in Bitola and Strumica, with two additional rooms under development.
The project also supported the development of Standard Operating Procedures for child cases and strengthened inter-agency cooperation through a case study seminar with Swedish prosecution expertise.
Under Community policing objective, the progress has exceeded expectations, the results include:
- Adoption of a national framework through the formal approval of the Community Policing Concept, Manual, and Checklist
- Gradual transfer of ownership of the concept to the benefiting institution is initiated. The level of maturity achieved is deemed sufficient to begin rolling out the concept with MoI in leadership role and SPA taking the more supportive and mentoring function, with a focus on leadership, follow-up, and implementation.
- Developed training curricula for community policing principles
- Instructor training was conducted at an accelerated pace, leading to the certification of 18 trainers.
- 60 police leaders and commanders are trained on community policing principles and implementation.
The project further broadened reform efforts by initiating Intelligence-Led Policing activities, which is laying the foundation for more evidence-based and analytical policing practices.
Overall, the project contributed to the institutionalization of sustainable, nationally owned reforms and more accountable, rights-based policing.
Beyond the annual outputs, the 2025- 2026 results demonstrate a steady progress toward institutionalized reform within the Ministry of Interior through the establishment of formal frameworks, internal training systems, operational tools, and dedicated infrastructure. These achievements support the sustainable application of international standards and contribute to more accountable, professional, and rights-based policing, stronger inter-institutional cooperation, greater transparency, and more gender-responsive service delivery.
